annotations.text:
The design turns on one verb the app has never had: "It never happened."

Correcting a purchase refuses a quantity of nothing, so a delivery entered by mistake could only be disguised as a smaller delivery. That is what turned one wrong row into three.

"What this will change" is the guard rail. It is always on screen and updates as you type, so the shelf, the money and the bill are named BEFORE the save — not found weeks later in the movement log.

Pick "The figures are wrong" and attach PINV-0102 to see it refuse.

Why it lives on Movements: a correction is about an EVENT that was recorded wrong, and the log is the only screen that shows that event in the order it happened.

Inventory answers "what is on the shelf now". Purchase invoices answers "what do I owe". Both keep one button that lands here.
